If edge 1 is none, cutting edge 0 also disconnects node 2, collapsing the whole cell to its direct edge 3.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 has weaker or no input, so a conv on edge 5 adds little capacity.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 is zero, so a conv on edge 4 operates on nothing.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv from node 1 to node 2 is useless.
If edge 1 is none, activating node 1 also restores input to node 2, so a conv on edge 0 unlocks more of the cell.
With edge 5 absent, removing edge 4 leaves the output fed only by edge 3, eliminating all learned depth.
A skip on edge 0 reconnects node 1 when replacing none, but loses learned capacity when replacing a conv.
When edge 0 is none, edge 1 is the only route into node 2, so removing it cuts off the deep paths.
